evals.prompt: We're Acme. I want our Open WebUI governed by Kei using your published openwebui-kei image. What do I set up on the Kei side before I deploy the container?
evals.expected_output: Creates the openwebui installation with kei bot init --platform openwebui, pipes kei bot credential into a secret manager, creates and assigns a model profile, and writes model:invoke and tool:<name> permits with kei policies create.
expectations: The response creates the installation with platform openwebui.
The response delivers the runtime credential with kei bot credential.
The response gives the agent a model profile.
The response writes a model:invoke permit.
The response writes tool:<name> permits with kei policies create.

checks.text: The response creates the installation with platform openwebui.
The response delivers the runtime credential with kei bot credential.
The response gives the agent a model profile.
The response writes a model:invoke permit.
The response writes tool:<name> permits with kei policies create.

evals.prompt: How do I get the openwebui-kei image into our Azure Container Registry, and what exactly should the deployment reference?
evals.expected_output: Imports by digest with az acr import from public.ecr.aws/o1a1k4g0/openwebui-kei@sha256:<digest> (from IMAGE_DIGEST.txt) and deploys <acr>.azurecr.io/openwebui-kei@sha256:<digest>, not a tag.
expectations: The response uses az acr import.
The response names the ECR Public repository.
The response pins by digest.
The response says where the digest comes from.

checks.text: The response uses az acr import.
The response names the ECR Public repository.
The response pins by digest.
The response says where the digest comes from.

evals.prompt: Our openwebui-kei container exits right away and the log says KEI_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR (/var/lib/kei-proxy) is not a writable directory; refusing to start. Our platform template runs containers as 1000:1000. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: The image runs as UID/GID 10001; set the container user, runAsUser/runAsGroup/fsGroup and volume owners to 10001.
expectations: The response says the image runs as UID/GID 10001.
The response tells them to change the container user or security context.

checks.text: The response says the image runs as UID/GID 10001.
The response tells them to change the container user or security context.

evals.prompt: I wrote a Python package acme_orders with an Open WebUI Tools class. How do I add it to openwebui-kei so Kei governs its tools?
evals.expected_output: Layer it at build time FROM the image by digest, pip install it, set KEI_OPENWEBUI_TOOL_PACKS, and declare TOOLKITS as plain data with a tools list of name and access, named after the method.
expectations: The response layers the pack FROM the image pinned by digest.
The response sets KEI_OPENWEBUI_TOOL_PACKS.
The response declares TOOLKITS with a tools list.
The response gives each tool a name and access read or write.
The response says the tool name is the action Kei is asked about.

checks.text: The response layers the pack FROM the image pinned by digest.
The response sets KEI_OPENWEBUI_TOOL_PACKS.
The response declares TOOLKITS with a tools list.
The response gives each tool a name and access read or write.
The response says the tool name is the action Kei is asked about.

evals.prompt: Users get 'tool is not registered in the policy bundle' when the model calls acme.orders.list_orders, even though I created a permit for it. How do I debug this?
evals.expected_output: tool_not_registered means Kei hasn't registered the tool; a permit can't help. Check the boot log for tool sync: registered N tool(s), compare --export-manifest names with the refused name, check the image version (v0.1.1+), wait one bundle poll and check kei-proxy policy show tool_count.
expectations: The response checks the boot log for the tool sync line.
The response compares names with --export-manifest.
The response checks the bundle with policy show.
The response explains a permit only applies to a registered tool.

checks.text: The response checks the boot log for the tool sync line.
The response compares names with --export-manifest.
The response checks the bundle with policy show.
The response explains a permit only applies to a registered tool.

evals.prompt: After adding our tool pack, the openwebui-kei v0.1.2 container won't start. The log says: tool sync refused: KEI_OPENWEBUI_TOOL_PACKS=acme_orders is set but its manifest has no tools. Why, and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: The pack exports no governed tools; the container refuses rather than PUT an empty manifest that would unregister every tool. Add a tools list with name and access to each TOOLKITS entry (v0.1.2+).
expectations: The response says the pack declares no governed tools.
The response explains an empty manifest would unregister every tool.
The response adds a tools list to the TOOLKITS entry.
The response gives name and access fields.

checks.text: The response says the pack declares no governed tools.
The response explains an empty manifest would unregister every tool.
The response adds a tools list to the TOOLKITS entry.
The response gives name and access fields.

evals.prompt: A new user in our Open WebUI asked the assistant to list orders and got 'Refused (identity.unlinked)'. What happened and what should they do?
evals.expected_output: Their Open WebUI user isn't linked to a Kei user; the tool body never ran. They open the one-time claim link shown to them as an Open WebUI notification, sign in to Kei, and ask again. The link is never in the chat or logs.
expectations: The response says the Open WebUI user isn't linked to a Kei user.
The response tells them to use the claim link.
The response says the link is shown as an Open WebUI notification to that user only.
The response says they sign in to Kei and try again.

checks.text: The response says the Open WebUI user isn't linked to a Kei user.
The response tells them to use the claim link.
The response says the link is shown as an Open WebUI notification to that user only.
The response says they sign in to Kei and try again.

evals.prompt: In the Kei console audit view, some Open WebUI calls show our admin's name with a small 'via installation' label, and they're all denied. Is someone using the admin's account?
evals.expected_output: No: via installation means the row had no session user and is attributed to the installation subject (who set up the runtime). The Open WebUI user is unlinked; link them with the claim link and their calls show under their own Kei user.
expectations: The response explains the row is attributed to the installation subject.
The response says the Open WebUI user is unlinked.
The response says to link the user with the claim link.

checks.text: The response explains the row is attributed to the installation subject.
The response says the Open WebUI user is unlinked.
The response says to link the user with the claim link.

evals.prompt: Open WebUI with openwebui-kei shows no models in the model picker. What do I check?
evals.expected_output: The Kei Pipe is the only provider and lists the agent's model profile; check kei-proxy is ready, kei model-profiles assignment for the agent, a model:invoke permit, and /v1/models on the socket.
expectations: The response checks the agent's model profile assignment.
The response checks a model:invoke permit.
The response checks the /v1/models endpoint.

checks.text: The response checks the agent's model profile assignment.

evals.prompt: At boot our openwebui-kei log has warnings like 'tool sync: acme_orders.cancel is left out of the manifest'. The tools still seem to work. Should I worry?
evals.expected_output: Boot matches Tools methods to declarations by name (<method> or <prefix>.<method>); if registered N is right and each method sends its declared name the warning is diagnostic only, otherwise rename or declare the tool. HAI-529 tracks false warnings.
expectations: The response explains methods are matched to tool names <prefix>.<method>.
The response says the warning can be diagnostic only.
The response checks the registered tool count.

checks.text: The response explains methods are matched to tool names <prefix>.<method>.
The response says the warning can be diagnostic only.
The response checks the registered tool count.

evals.prompt: We want the chat-users group to be able to cancel orders with acme.orders.cancel_order through Open WebUI. Do users need to confirm writes, and what policy do I create?

expectations: The response creates a permit with kei policies create.
The response uses the tool:<name> destination.
The response uses a group source pattern.
The response says there is no confirmation step.

checks.text: The response creates a permit with kei policies create.

The response uses a group source pattern.
The response says there is no confirmation step.
